newsitem.title: USA: Truck overturns, explosion threat in North Carolina.
newsitem.headline: Truck overturns, explosion threat in North Carolina.

text.p: Authorities cordoned off a stretch of North Carolina countryside Wednesday after a dump truck carrying 15,000 pounds of ammonium nitrate fertiliser, diesel fuel and other explosive substances overturned on a local highway.
Highway Patrol Lt. J.E. Smith said the truck overturned between the towns of Princeton and Goldsboro in the eastern portion of the state while on its way to a rock quarry at about 7 a.m. EDT.
He said the cargo would cause a powerful explosion if it were detonated but there was little actual risk. "We do not anticipate an explosion," Smith said.

Ammonium nitrate is the fertiliser used in the bombing of the federal building in Oklahoma City in 1995. An emergency worker said the truck's cargo, if detonated, could generate an explosion five times as strong as that blast.
A three-mile square stretch of the sparsely populated area was cordoned off and part of the highway was closed for several hours as a precaution, Smith said.
